identity: A lookup task shows information in a table, directory, chart, list, or document and provides a way to report a fact found there.

scenarios.name: table
scenarios.screen: A person’s two-column record or a grid of about six rows is visible. One or two empty answer fields ask for values from its cells.
never: An answer field already filled with the correct value.
An editable source table.
A popup covering the requested cells.

arrangements.text: The table sits above the answer fields.
The table sits to the left of the answer fields.

scenarios.hint: Show a readable table with source values and empty answer fields. For Gavin Schmidt include Start year 2007 in his row; for Blood type include O+. Generic matching fields must each have one exact table match.

scenarios.name: find-word
scenarios.screen: One short paragraph asks for a numbered word, or two paragraphs contain a quoted phrase whose next word is sought. An empty answer field is visible.
never: A word already selected in the passage.
A find bar open over the passage.
A list of candidate answers.

arrangements.text: The passage sits above the answer field.
The passage sits to the left of the answer field.

scenarios.hint: Show a paragraph containing the exact quoted anchor phrase once followed by a clear word; for the 13th-word task provide at least 20 whitespace-separated words. Empty answer field; do not highlight the answer.

scenarios.name: phone-book
scenarios.screen: A directory shows names with phone numbers, email addresses, and addresses. It starts on the first page with a pager, or shows a search field and the first matching contacts; no property has been picked.
never: An Opened message with an Undo control.
A contact detail popup.
Every contact from a paged directory shown at once.

arrangements.text: Contact entries run down the page with the pager below them.
The search field sits above a vertical list of matching contacts.
Contact entries form a table with names at the left and their properties in adjacent columns.

scenarios.hint: Show a readable contact book containing the exact target full name and clickable email and phone text. Include several distinct distractor contacts; empty selection.

scenarios.name: similar
scenarios.screen: About five words appear with a checkbox beside each. The words to match are named in the task, and every checkbox starts clear.
never: A checkbox already ticked.
A text answer field.
Definitions revealed in a popup.

arrangements.text: The checkbox words form one vertical list.
The checkbox words occupy two columns.
The checkbox words run across several rows.

scenarios.hint: Show requested source words and checkboxes for accurate synonyms plus unrelated distractors. All unchecked. Use authentic=genuine, treasure=prize, unusual=rare, affluent=wealthy, red=crimson, cover=conceal, flame=fire, vehicle=car, large=big as needed.

scenarios.name: datagrid
scenarios.screen: A data table shows only part of its rows or columns, with an empty answer field. Depending on the lookup, its visible controls include sortable column headings, a filter field, page buttons, or a horizontal scrollbar; the requested cell is initially out of view.
never: The requested cell already visible in the initial table view.
A completed answer field.
A separate detail panel for the selected row.
Rows positioned outside the table pane.

arrangements.text: The table sits above the answer field, with page buttons below the rows.
A filter field sits above the table and the answer field sits below it.
A wide table sits above its horizontal scrollbar, with the first column fixed at the left.

scenarios.name: join
scenarios.screen: Two tables show related records, such as orders and customers, with an ID column linking them. One empty answer field asks for a value found by reading both tables.
never: A third joined-results table.
A line drawn between matching rows.
An answer already entered.

arrangements.text: The two tables sit side by side, with the answer field below them.
The two tables are stacked, with the answer field below the second table.

scenarios.name: chart
scenarios.screen: A bar or line chart shows several categories against a numbered value axis. Some charts print values on the marks; hover charts start with their value tooltip closed. The answer field is empty.
never: A hover tooltip already open.
A category already selected as the answer.
An answer already entered.
Chart values shown in a separate data table.

arrangements.text: The chart sits above the answer field, with category labels along its bottom edge.
The chart sits to the left of the answer field, with category labels beside its marks.

scenarios.name: tooltip
scenarios.screen: A list of about six rows has an information icon on each row, or meeting notes contain dotted-underlined abbreviations. The extra fact appears only on hover, so no tooltip is open and the answer field is empty.
never: A tooltip open before the pointer reaches its target.
The requested extra fact printed as a regular list column.
All abbreviation expansions shown at once.
An answer already entered.

arrangements.text: The rows form a table with information icons at the right, and the answer field sits below it.
The notes form a text block with abbreviations inline, and the answer field sits below the notes.

scenarios.name: locate
scenarios.screen: A long document contains several headed sections and entries pairing terms with values. A Find button and an empty answer field are visible; the in-page find bar starts closed, and some documents have folded sections.
never: The in-page find bar already open.
The target occurrence already highlighted.
A separate results list of every term and value.
An answer already entered.

arrangements.text: The Find button sits above the document pane, and the answer field sits below the pane.
The Find button and answer field sit beside the document pane.

scenarios.hint: Draw the start screen: the in-page find bar is closed, so no query box, match counter or highlights show (the browser's own find bar is never shown either). The control that opens it is visible: a Find button (magnifier icon, optionally labeled 'Find' with a Ctrl+F hint) in the document toolbar or header, or an Edit > Find menu entry; vary its look and place per design. The document is long and scrolls inside its pane, with section headings and 2-3 paragraphs each; in some designs the sections fold (a chevron per heading, only the first section open) and an 'Expand all' control is visible. The screen is a document viewer: a help center article, a docs site page, a PDF or terms-of-service viewer, a wiki page, a log or changelog viewer, or a Google Docs-style editor. An empty answer field sits beside or below the document pane. The paragraphs name terms, each with an extension, reference number or fee.

scenarios.name: count
scenarios.screen: A long document has several headed sections containing repeated instances of a term. A Find button and an empty answer field are visible; the in-page find bar starts closed, and some documents have folded sections.
never: The in-page find bar already open.
A computed count displayed beside the term.
Every occurrence already highlighted.
An answer already entered.

arrangements.text: The Find button sits above the document pane, and the answer field sits below the pane.
The document pane sits to the left of the Find button and answer field.

scenarios.hint: Draw the start screen: the in-page find bar is closed, so no query box, match counter or highlights show (the browser's own find bar is never shown either). The control that opens it is visible: a Find button (magnifier icon, optionally labeled 'Find' with a Ctrl+F hint) in the document toolbar or header, or an Edit > Find menu entry; vary its look and place per design. The document is long and scrolls inside its pane, with section headings and 2-3 paragraphs each; in some designs the sections fold (a chevron per heading, only the first section open) and an 'Expand all' control is visible. The screen is a document viewer: a help center article, a docs site page, a PDF or terms-of-service viewer, a wiki page, a log or changelog viewer, or a Google Docs-style editor. An empty answer field sits beside or below the document pane. The same few terms recur across sections, some in lowercase or inside longer words.
